transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... people have been telling me they can actually see something's off with how I'm moving. Like I'm moving like I'm underwater, you know? Taking forever to just answer a question or even get out of a chair. Which is weird because usually I'm pretty quick. I work in customer service, so you have to be fast on the phones. Sometimes I get these callers who just want to complain about the shipping times, and I'm like, "Ma'am, I don't drive the delivery truck." But anyway, yeah, either I'm super slow, or else I'm just pacing my apartment for hours, rubbing my hands together like I'm trying to shake off a bad call. It's really frustrating. My cat, Mr. Whiskers, he just sits there watching me pace. I think he judges me, honestly. He's an orange tabby, very vocal. But yeah, the moving too slow or too fast thing is why I'm here.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day?

Depressed? I don't really think so... I mean, I haven't noticed feeling sad most of the day or anything like that. Though I do get a little bummed out when I see those sad animal rescue commercials, you know the ones with the Sarah McLachlan song? Man, those are just brutal. Mr. Whiskers usually just leaves the room when they come on. I actually ended up upgrading my streaming service to the ad-free tier just to avoid them entirely. It's like four extra dollars a month, which doesn't sound like a lot, but when you add up Netflix, Hulu, and all the others, you're basically just paying for cable all over again. My buddy Mark was just complaining about that the other day. He works in IT and keeps trying to show me how to pirate movies, but I really don't want to risk getting a virus on my work laptop, you know? The IT department at my job is super strict about what we do on our machines, and if I get locked out, I can't take any calls. But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling depressed. Yeah, no, I don't really feel like that.
Have you had a time when you felt unusually energetic or high?

Energetic or high? No, not really. I mean, I drink a lot of coffee, but that's just because I work the early shift. I have to be logged on by 7 AM, which means I'm up at 5:30. I got this new coffee maker, actually, one of those fancy ones that grinds the beans right before it brews. It's supposed to be better for the flavor profile or whatever. My sister got it for me for my birthday. She's really into all that artisanal stuff. She actually lives in Portland now, which makes sense, right? Everyone there is super into coffee and, like, knitting their own sweaters. She keeps trying to get me to come visit, but flights are just so expensive right now. I was looking on Expedia the other day, and even with the budget airlines, it's crazy. Plus, you have to pay for carry-on bags now! Can you believe that? It's like they nickel and dime you for everything. I remember when you could just bring a bag and they'd even give you a little pack of peanuts. Now you're lucky if you get a half-cup of water. But, uh, yeah, no, I don't get unusually energetic or anything like that. Just the normal caffeine buzz, you know?
Have you been hearing voices that other people can't hear?

Voices? Well... it's kind of weird you bring that up. I actually have been hearing stuff from work when I'm not even working. Like, I'll hear my old headset beep—you know that little electronic chime it makes when a call drops in?—and then I'll hear this supervisor-type voice just say my name, or tell me I'm being "too slow." And the thing is, my laptop is completely closed and there’s no phone ringing at all. 

It's really annoying because supervisors are always on you about being too slow anyway. My old manager, Greg, he used to monitor our average handle times like a hawk. He had this massive Excel spreadsheet, color-coded and everything. I don't know how these middle managers have the time to just stare at spreadsheets all day, you know? Like, don't you have actual work to do? He would literally ping me on Teams if my wrap-up time went over thirty seconds. Wrap-up time is when you type the notes after a call, and you have to be really detailed, otherwise the next rep gets completely confused when the customer calls back. And the system we use is so clunky, it takes forever to load the customer's profile anyway, so it's not even my fault if it takes a minute. But yeah... I'll just be sitting there in my living room with the computer shut, and I'll hear that beep and the voice getting on my case.
Have the voices ever happened during a time when you were not depressed or unusually energetic?

Yeah, actually... I've had stretches, like a few weeks here and there, where my mood was totally fine. Like, closer to normal, and I was actually getting things done around the apartment. I even finally cleaned out the lint trap in my dryer. You know how dangerous those things are? My buddy Mark—the IT guy I mentioned—his cousin's entire apartment building almost burned down because someone didn't clean their lint trap. It's crazy how something so small can cause so much damage. It's like those little space heaters people bring into the office during the winter because the AC is always blasting. I used to sit right under a vent at my last job, and I swear I had a cold from October to March. I brought in this little ceramic heater, and Greg—my old manager—made me take it home because it was a "fire hazard." Meanwhile, the microwave in the breakroom sparked every time someone tried to heat up a Hot Pocket, but that was totally fine, apparently. Hot Pockets are terrible for you anyway, just pure sodium. But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right. Even during those good weeks when I'm feeling fine and getting stuff done, I still hear that supervisor voice. Or I'll just feel absolutely certain that the old ticketing software is flagging my account for some reason, even when I'm not working.
Have you ever had a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt rested?

Less sleep? No, I usually need my full eight hours, otherwise I'm completely useless the next day. Sometimes nine if I can swing it. I actually bought this really nice weighted blanket a few months ago to help me sleep better. It's like fifteen pounds, which sounds heavy, but it's supposed to simulate a hug or something? I don't know the exact science behind it, but it really works. My buddy Mark told me about it. He's always researching random biohacking stuff. Like last month, he was trying to convince me to start taking these mushroom supplements—not the psychedelic kind, just like, lion's mane or whatever. He said it improves cognitive function and helps with brain fog. But I don't know, those supplements are completely unregulated by the FDA. You could be taking literally anything. I watched this documentary on Netflix about the supplement industry, and it's wild. They can basically put whatever they want in those capsules as long as they don't claim it cures a disease. It's just like the diet pill craze in the 90s, remember that? People were having heart attacks from ephedra. My aunt tried all those crazy diets back then. Cabbage soup, grapefruit... she even did that one where you only eat meat and cheese. But yeah, no, I definitely need my sleep. I've never had a time where I didn't need it.
Have you ever had a period of at least a few days when you felt unusually irritable?

Irritable? I mean... I don't think so. Not unusually, anyway. Like, I'll get annoyed at normal things, but I've never had days where I'm just snapping at everyone for no reason. Though, speaking of getting annoyed, the traffic around my apartment complex has been absolutely insane lately. They decided to repave the main road right at the entrance, and they only have one lane open. So you have to sit there waiting for this guy with a stop sign to flip it to "slow." And half the time, the guy isn't even paying attention. He's just looking at his phone. I swear, nobody has any work ethic anymore. It's just like when I call my internet provider. I was on hold for forty-five minutes last Tuesday because my Wi-Fi kept dropping. Forty-five minutes! And when I finally got someone, they just told me to unplug the router and plug it back in. Like I hadn't already tried that ten times. It's a standard script, I know, I used to do it, but come on. And then they try to upsell you on a faster package while your current one doesn't even work. It's a total scam. Cable companies basically have a monopoly in most areas, so they can treat you however they want. My buddy Mark actually set up his own mesh network at his house, and he says he never has dead zones anymore. I might have him come over and help me set one up. But um, yeah, no, I wouldn't say I get unusually irritable. Just the normal amount when things are frustrating.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?

Depressed for two weeks straight? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I get down sometimes, sure, but not like every single day for weeks. It's more like... I'll just have a bad day here and there. Like last week, I was feeling pretty bummed out because I went to the grocery store to get those specific jalapeño kettle chips I like, and they were completely sold out. Again. It's the third time this month. I don't understand how a major grocery chain can't keep their inventory stocked properly. It's all automated now, right? The system should know when they're running low and just order more. My buddy Mark was telling me about this new supply chain software his company is implementing, and it uses AI to predict buying patterns based on weather and local events. Like, if it's going to rain, it automatically orders more umbrellas and soup. It's actually kind of creepy when you think about it. The computers know what we want before we even know we want it. It's just like how you talk about something near your phone, and suddenly you're getting ads for it on Instagram. I was literally just talking to my mom about getting a new coffee maker, and bam, ten different ads for espresso machines. I don't even drink espresso, it makes my heart race too much. But yeah, no, I haven't been depressed like that. Just regular bad days, you know?
Have you had any recent seizures?

Seizures? No, definitely not. I've never had anything like that happen to me. My cousin's dog actually has seizures, though. It's really sad. He's this little Jack Russell terrier mix, super high energy usually, but then he'll just drop and start shaking. They have him on some kind of medication for it now, pheno-something, I think? But they have to hide the pill in a scoop of peanut butter or he'll just spit it right back out. Dogs are so smart like that. Like, they know when you're trying to trick them. My old roommate had a cat that figured out how to open the cabinets in the kitchen. We'd wake up and all the Tupperware would be all over the floor. We had to put child locks on everything, which was honestly super annoying because I could barely figure out how to open them myself when I was half asleep trying to get a bowl for cereal. I'm a big cereal guy. Cinnamon Toast Crunch is top tier, but honestly, a good bowl of Honey Nut Cheerios just hits different sometimes. Mark says cereal is basically just eating dessert for breakfast because of all the sugar, but whatever. Anyway, no, no seizures for me.
Have you ever had a serious brain injury or a neurological illness?

Brain injury? Um... no, I've never hit my head that hard or had any neurological stuff. I mean, I bumped my head on the open trunk of my car a couple weeks ago, but that was just because I was rushing to get my groceries inside before the ice cream melted. It was that really hot day we had, remember? Like 95 degrees in early May, which is just ridiculous. I bought this new brand of pistachio gelato, and it was pretty expensive, so I didn't want it turning into soup. I actually watched a documentary the other night about how gelato is made differently than regular ice cream. They churn it slower, so there's less air whipped into it, which makes it denser and more flavorful. Plus they serve it at a slightly warmer temperature so your taste buds don't get numbed by the cold. It's fascinating how much science goes into food. Like baking—baking is basically just chemistry. If you mess up the ratio of baking soda to flour, your cookies turn out like little hockey pucks. My mom used to make these incredible chocolate chip cookies when I was a kid, but she never wrote the recipe down. She just kind of threw things in a bowl. I tried to recreate them once, and I totally forgot the vanilla extract. You wouldn't think one little teaspoon of liquid would make such a huge difference, but they tasted completely flat. Anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right, brain injuries. Yeah, no, nothing serious like that. Just the occasional bump on a car trunk.
Have the voices and those strong beliefs about the work software happened for at least a month during a time when your mood was otherwise normal?

Well, yeah, actually. There have been stretches, like a few weeks here and there, where I actually felt pretty okay. My mood was closer to normal, I was getting up, getting things done around the apartment, doing my laundry... which, by the way, the dryer in my building is completely useless right now. You have to run it through three cycles just to get a load of towels dry. I told the landlord about it, but he's always dragging his feet. He says it's an issue with the lint trap ventilation or something, but I think he just doesn't want to pay for a repair guy. Repair guys charge like, what, a hundred bucks just to show up? It's a total racket. My uncle used to do HVAC repair, and he told me half the time he'd just go to a house, clean off a sensor with a Q-tip, and charge them for a full service call. He said people just don't want to learn how their own appliances work. It's like cars. I don't know the first thing about cars. If my check engine light comes on, I just put a piece of black electrical tape over it so it stops glaring at me at night. But anyway, yeah, even during those couple of weeks when I was feeling fine and getting my chores done, I still heard that supervisor voice talking to me. And I was still completely sure that the old ticketing software at work was flagging my account. So the mood stuff was fine, but the other stuff was definitely still happening.
Have you found yourself holding the same body position for a long time, even when it would be uncomfortable?

Um... holding the same position? I mean, I guess sometimes when I get really overwhelmed with everything, I'll kind of just freeze up. Like, I'll catch myself standing in the kitchen with my coffee mug just hovering halfway to my mouth, and I won't even realize how long I've been standing there. Or I'll start walking this same little loop back and forth by the couch for no real reason. I actually got that couch at a thrift store, believe it or not. It's this really cool mid-century modern style, kind of a mustard yellow color. Mark hated it when I first brought it home. He said it looked like it belonged in a 1970s bowling alley, but I think it gives the living room character. Plus, it's surprisingly comfortable once you break it in. The only problem is the fabric is a magnet for pet hair, which is weird because I don't even have any pets. But somehow, every time I sit down in black sweatpants, I stand up looking like I just hugged a golden retriever. I've gone through so many of those sticky lint rollers. The ones from the dollar store are terrible, by the way. The paper just rips in these tiny diagonal strips instead of peeling off in one clean sheet, so you spend ten minutes just trying to find the edge. It's infuriating. But yeah, sometimes I just stand there with my coffee, or do the pacing thing by the couch when things feel like too much.
Has anyone noticed that you resist when they try to move your body or get you to do something, even when you’re able to move?

Resist when they try to move me? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, nobody's really tried to physically move me around like that. I live by myself, so there's not really anyone around to do that anyway. It's just me and the apartment, which honestly is getting a little cramped. I've been thinking about trying to find a bigger place, maybe something with a balcony. I saw this one listing online the other day that had this amazing little terrace overlooking a courtyard, but the rent was just outrageous. It's crazy how much they charge for a tiny square of outdoor space in this city. And the deposit they wanted was equal to two months' rent, plus a non-refundable application fee. Application fees are such a scam. You pay fifty bucks just for them to run a credit check that costs them like two dollars, and then they don't even call you back if they pick someone else. I had a friend who spent almost three hundred dollars just applying to places before she finally got one. She works at a bakery downtown—well, she used to, before they downsized. She made these amazing sourdough loaves. Sourdough is so tricky to get right, you have to feed the starter every day and keep it at the perfect temperature. If it gets too cold, the yeast just kind of goes to sleep and the bread turns out flat. I tried making it once during that phase when everyone was baking bread, but my starter just smelled like old gym socks, so I threw it out. But anyway, no, nobody has tried to physically move me or anything like that. I just do my own thing.
Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually important or powerful?

Important or powerful? No, definitely not. I mean, I'm just a customer service rep, you know? You pretty much feel like the least important person on the planet when you're doing that job. People call in and yell at you over the smallest things, acting like *they're* the king of the world. Like this one guy last week, he was screaming at me because his account update was delayed by an hour. An hour! And it's not like I personally control the servers. 

Speaking of servers, my laptop has been acting so weird lately. The fan just spins up and sounds like an airplane taking off, even when I only have one browser tab open. I think it might be full of dust. I tried to buy one of those cans of compressed air to clean it out, but they lock them up behind glass at the pharmacy now. You have to press a little red button and wait for an employee to come unlock it. I stood there for like fifteen minutes the other day, pressing the button, and the overhead speaker just kept saying "Customer assistance needed in aisle four." Over and over. Nobody ever came. I ended up just giving up and buying a candy bar at the front register instead. It was one of those ones with the almonds in it. I usually prefer peanuts, but peanuts have been giving me heartburn lately. Actually, almost everything gives me heartburn lately, which sucks because I love spicy food. There's this great Thai place down the street... 

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, feeling powerful. Yeah, no, I don't get feelings like that. I'm just a regular guy.
Have the voices and your certainty that the work software was flagging you been going on for at least a month?

Um, a month? No, it's been a lot longer than that. I think... yeah, it's been about a year and eight months now that I've been hearing them and knowing the software is watching me. And it's not just when I'm feeling really down or anything, it's just kind of always there. 

Like, even when I had that brief period where I tried to get back into running—which didn't last long, by the way. I bought these really expensive running shoes, the kind with the extra thick foam on the bottom that are supposed to be like running on clouds. They were neon green. I thought maybe a bright color would motivate me to put them on in the mornings. But the laces were those weird elastic ones that you don't tie, you just pull them tight with a little plastic toggle thing. I could never get the tension right. They were either cutting off the circulation to my toes or slipping off my heel with every step. I ended up getting this massive blister on my right heel after just two miles. Blisters are the worst, especially when you have to wear dress shoes for a cousin's wedding or something. My cousin Sarah got married last October in this beautiful outdoor ceremony, but it rained the whole time. They had to rent this huge tent at the last minute, and the ground was so muddy. Everyone's shoes were ruined. They had a taco bar for the reception, though, which was pretty cool. I love tacos, especially the al pastor kind with the little pieces of pineapple mixed in. The sweetness really balances out the spice. 

But yeah, anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the voices and the software thing. Yeah, it's been going on for like a year and eight months, not just when I'm super depressed.
Do you ever go completely mute and stop speaking for a while, even when people are talking to you?

Go mute? Like, just stop talking entirely? No, I don't think so. I mean, I talk all day for my job, so I can't really get away with that. Though sometimes I definitely wish I could just hit a mute button on myself, or on the customers. My throat gets so dry by the end of my shift. I started drinking that throat coat tea, the one with the slippery elm in it? It's supposed to be really good for your vocal cords, but it tastes exactly like black licorice. 

I absolutely hate black licorice. When I was a kid, my grandma used to keep this crystal bowl of black jelly beans on her coffee table. Who even likes the black jelly beans? They just sat there for years, I swear they were practically fossilized. Her house always smelled like mothballs and peppermint. She had this massive grandfather clock in the hallway that chimed every fifteen minutes, day and night. It drove me crazy when I had to sleep over. The pendulum was made of this really shiny brass, and I remember trying to polish it with my sleeve once. Brass tarnishes so fast if you don't keep up with it. I have a brass lamp on my desk right now, actually, and it's looking pretty dull. I should probably buy some Brasso. You can get it at the hardware store, but the mom-and-pop hardware store near my apartment just closed down last month. They're turning it into a boutique pet bakery. A bakery for dogs! Can you believe people spend eight dollars on a cupcake for a pug? It's wild. 

But anyway... no, I don't ever just go completely mute. I always answer when people talk to me, even if it's just to say yeah or whatever.
Have you lost interest in being around other people?

Lost interest? I guess... I mean, my friends keep telling me I sound totally flat these days, like I'm hard to read or something. And even when they're talking about stuff I actually care about, I just end up giving these really short answers and I avoid making plans to hang out. 

Making plans is just so exhausting anyway. You have to coordinate schedules, and then someone always cancels at the last minute because they forgot they had a dentist appointment. I hate the dentist. The last time I went, the hygienist kept talking to me while she had her hands in my mouth. How are you supposed to answer when someone has a metal hook scraping your molars? She was telling me all about her son's travel baseball team. Travel sports are so intense now. Parents spend thousands of dollars just so their ten-year-old can play in tournaments three states away every weekend. It's ridiculous. I played little league when I was a kid, but we just played at the park down the street. The snack shack there had the best soft pretzels. They were always super salty, and they came with this little plastic cup of neon yellow cheese. I used to dip my pretzels in it until the cheese was totally gone, and then I'd try to scrape the rest out with my finger. You can't really get good pretzels like that anymore, except maybe at the mall. But the mall is always so crowded, especially around the holidays. The parking lot is a nightmare... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, being around people. Yeah, I just kind of keep to myself and give short answers now. I don't really make plans with anyone.
When you freeze like that, do you stay in the exact same position for a long time even if it becomes uncomfortable?

Freeze in the same position? I mean... I don't know about staying completely frozen like a statue for a really long time. But when I get really overwhelmed with everything, I do catch myself doing weird things. Like, I'll be standing in the kitchen with my coffee mug just hovering halfway to my mouth, just kind of stuck there. Or I'll find myself walking the exact same little loop around my couch over and over for no real reason. 

My couch is this dark gray sectional I got off Craigslist a couple years ago. The guy who sold it to me said it was barely used, but there's definitely a dip in the middle cushion where you can tell someone sat all the time. It came with these terrible mustard yellow throw pillows that I immediately threw in the closet. Mustard yellow is just such an aggressive color, you know? It reminds me of the uniform I had to wear at my first job in high school. I worked at this hot dog stand at the local fairgrounds. We had to wear these bright yellow polo shirts with a cartoon hot dog embroidered on the pocket. The hot dog was wearing sunglasses and giving a thumbs up. It was so embarrassing. The worst part was that the stand didn't have air conditioning, and in August it would get up to like a hundred degrees in there. The smell of boiling hot dogs and stale buns just baked into my clothes. I must have washed that uniform a hundred times, but I could never get the smell out. I actually had to throw the shirts away when I quit because even my mom said they were making the whole laundry room smell like cheap meat. I haven't been able to eat a hot dog since then. 

But yeah, what were we talking about? Oh, freezing. Yeah, I just kind of get stuck holding my coffee or pacing around the couch sometimes when it's all too much.
Has anyone ever placed your arms or body into a position and then you stayed that way for a while?

Placed my arms in a position? Like... like someone else moving my body for me? No, nobody does that. I live by myself, so there's no one around to even try that, you know? It's just me and my cat, Barnaby. 

Barnaby is a Maine Coon mix, so he's absolutely massive. He's got these giant tufted ears and paws the size of baseballs. He's actually the reason I had to buy a new vacuum cleaner last month. He sheds so much, it's like a second cat is forming on my rug every week. I ended up getting one of those Dyson stick vacuums. They're so expensive, but everyone says they're the best. I don't know though, the battery only lasts like twenty minutes on the highest setting. By the time I finish the living room and the hallway, it's dead. Then I have to wait three hours for it to charge just so I can do my bedroom. It's so annoying. I should have just bought a regular plug-in one. My mom has this old Hoover from the nineties that still works perfectly. It's this ugly teal color, and it's super loud, but it sucks up everything. She used to make me vacuum the stairs every Saturday morning when I was a teenager. The cord was never quite long enough to reach all the way to the top, so I always had to unplug it halfway up and find another outlet. We lived in this split-level house, and the layout was just so weird. The kitchen was basically on a landing between the living room and the bedrooms...

Wait, sorry. No, nobody poses my arms or anything like that. I just move myself.
Have you ever repeated other people's words exactly after they say them?

Repeated other people's words? Like, repeating them back? No, I don't think I do that. Unless you count when I'm on the phone at work. I work in customer service for this internet provider, and we actually have to repeat the customer's issue back to them as part of our script. It's supposed to show "active listening" or whatever. So if they say, "My router keeps dropping the signal," I have to say, "I understand your router keeps dropping the signal." 

It honestly just makes people mad half the time. They think I'm being condescending. People get so angry about their internet. I had this one guy yell at me for twenty minutes last week because his Netflix was buffering. He kept saying he paid for high speed and I was personally stealing from him. He lived out in this super rural area, too. Like, you can't live in the middle of a forest and expect gigabit speeds, you know? I actually went camping in a forest once, up in the mountains. It was supposed to be this relaxing weekend, but it rained the entire time. The tent leaked, and all my extra socks got soaked. There is nothing worse than wet socks. We tried to make a fire, but the wood was completely saturated. We ended up just sitting in my friend's car eating cold cans of baked beans and listening to the radio. They were playing this weird marathon of 80s synth-pop... 

But no, I don't just repeat what people say to me in normal life. Just when my boss makes me.

doctor.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
doctor.question: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

target_item.name: Psychomotor_Changes
target_item.manifestation: I came in because people can actually see me either moving like I’m underwater, taking forever to answer or get out of a chair, or else pacing my apartment and rubbing my hands like I’m trying to shake off a bad call.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the item corresponding to the chief_complaint_symptom_code, which is S028.

patient.answer: Well, I came in because... people have been telling me they can actually see something's off with how I'm moving. Like I'm moving like I'm underwater, you know? Taking forever to just answer a question or even get out of a chair. Which is weird because usually I'm pretty quick. I work in customer service, so you have to be fast on the phones. Sometimes I get these callers who just want to complain about the shipping times, and I'm like, "Ma'am, I don't drive the delivery truck." But anyway, yeah, either I'm super slow, or else I'm just pacing my apartment for hours, rubbing my hands together like I'm trying to shake off a bad call. It's really frustrating. My cat, Mr. Whiskers, he just sits there watching me pace. I think he judges me, honestly. He's an orange tabby, very vocal. But yeah, the moving too slow or too fast thing is why I'm here.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychomotor changes are occurring in the context of a major depressive episode, which best distinguishes depressive disorders from bipolar, schizophrenia-spectrum, and organic causes.
doctor.question: Have you been feeling depressed most of the day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about depressed mood most of the day, which is a symptom of a major depressive episode. My symptom profile includes Loss of Interest, Weight/Appetite Change, Sleep Disturbance, Worthlessness/Guilt, and Negative Symptoms, but it does not have a specific entry for 'Depressed Mood' itself, only the duration and concurrent requirements of the depressive episode. Therefore, no direct match for 'depressed mood' exists in my profile.

patient.answer: Depressed? I don't really think so... I mean, I haven't noticed feeling sad most of the day or anything like that. Though I do get a little bummed out when I see those sad animal rescue commercials, you know the ones with the Sarah McLachlan song? Man, those are just brutal. Mr. Whiskers usually just leaves the room when they come on. I actually ended up upgrading my streaming service to the ad-free tier just to avoid them entirely. It's like four extra dollars a month, which doesn't sound like a lot, but when you add up Netflix, Hulu, and all the others, you're basically just paying for cable all over again. My buddy Mark was just complaining about that the other day. He works in IT and keeps trying to show me how to pirate movies, but I really don't want to risk getting a virus on my work laptop, you know? The IT department at my job is super strict about what we do on our machines, and if I get locked out, I can't take any calls. But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling depressed. Yeah, no, I don't really feel like that.

inference.note: Patient denies depressed mood, making severe depressive episodes less likely; psychomotor disturbance remains prominent, so depressive candidates F32.2 and F33.2 are deprioritized. Need further questioning to distinguish bipolar, schizophrenia spectrum, schizoaffective, or organic causes.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a distinct period of elevated or unusually energetic mood, which would help distinguish bipolar disorder from schizophrenia spectrum or catatonia due to a medical condition.

I got this new coffee maker, actually, one of those fancy ones that grinds the beans right before it brews. It's supposed to be better for the flavor profile or whatever. My sister got it for me for my birthday. She's really into all that artisanal stuff. She actually lives in Portland now, which makes sense, right? Everyone there is super into coffee and, like, knitting their own sweaters. She keeps trying to get me to come visit, but flights are just so expensive right now. patient.answer:
Voices? Well... it's kind of weird you bring that up. I actually have been hearing stuff from work when I'm not even working. Like, I'll hear my old headset beep—you know that little electronic chime it makes when a call drops in?—and then I'll hear this supervisor-type voice just say my name, or tell me I'm being "too slow." And the thing is, my laptop is completely closed and there’s no phone ringing at all. 

It's really annoying because supervisors are always on you about being too slow anyway. My old manager, Greg, he used to monitor our average handle times like a hawk. He had this massive Excel spreadsheet, color-coded and everything. I don't know how these middle managers have the time to just stare at spreadsheets all day, you know? Like, don't you have actual work to do? He would literally ping me on Teams if my wrap-up time went over thirty seconds. Wrap-up time is when you type the notes after a call, and you have to be really detailed, otherwise the next rep gets completely confused when the customer calls back. And the system we use is so clunky, it takes forever to load the customer's profile anyway, so it's not even my fault if it takes a minute. But yeah... I'll just be sitting there in my living room with the computer shut, and I'll hear that beep and the voice getting on my case.

Like, closer to normal, and I was actually getting things done around the apartment. I even finally cleaned out the lint trap in my dryer. You know how dangerous those things are? My buddy Mark—the IT guy I mentioned—his cousin's entire apartment building almost burned down because someone didn't clean their lint trap. It's crazy how something so small can cause so much damage. It's like those little space heaters people bring into the office during the winter because the AC is always blasting. I used to sit right under a vent at my last job, and I swear I had a cold from October to March. I brought in this little ceramic heater, and Greg—my old manager—made me take it home because it was a "fire hazard." Meanwhile, the microwave in the breakroom sparked every time someone tried to heat up a Hot Pocket, but that was totally fine, apparently. Hot Pockets are terrible for you anyway, just pure sodium. But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right. Even during those good weeks when I'm feeling fine and getting stuff done, I still hear that supervisor voice. I actually bought this really nice weighted blanket a few months ago to help me sleep better. It's like fifteen pounds, which sounds heavy, but it's supposed to simulate a hug or something? I don't know the exact science behind it, but it really works. My buddy Mark told me about it. He's always researching random biohacking stuff. Like last month, he was trying to convince me to start taking these mushroom supplements—not the psychedelic kind, just like, lion's mane or whatever. He said it improves cognitive function and helps with brain fog. But I don't know, those supplements are completely unregulated by the FDA. You could be taking literally anything. I watched this documentary on Netflix about the supplement industry, and it's wild. They can basically put whatever they want in those capsules as long as they don't claim it cures a disease. It's just like the diet pill craze in the 90s, remember that? People were having heart attacks from ephedra. My aunt tried all those crazy diets back then. Cabbage soup, grapefruit... she even did that one where you only eat meat and cheese. But yeah, no, I definitely need my sleep. I've never had a time where I didn't need it.

patient.answer: Irritable? I mean... I don't think so. Not unusually, anyway. Like, I'll get annoyed at normal things, but I've never had days where I'm just snapping at everyone for no reason. Though, speaking of getting annoyed, the traffic around my apartment complex has been absolutely insane lately. They decided to repave the main road right at the entrance, and they only have one lane open. So you have to sit there waiting for this guy with a stop sign to flip it to "slow." And half the time, the guy isn't even paying attention. He's just looking at his phone. I swear, nobody has any work ethic anymore. It's just like when I call my internet provider. I was on hold for forty-five minutes last Tuesday because my Wi-Fi kept dropping. Forty-five minutes! And when I finally got someone, they just told me to unplug the router and plug it back in. Like I hadn't already tried that ten times. It's a standard script, I know, I used to do it, but come on. And then they try to upsell you on a faster package while your current one doesn't even work. It's a total scam. Cable companies basically have a monopoly in most areas, so they can treat you however they want. My buddy Mark actually set up his own mesh network at his house, and he says he never has dead zones anymore. I might have him come over and help me set one up. But um, yeah, no, I wouldn't say I get unusually irritable. Just the normal amount when things are frustrating.

It's the third time this month. I don't understand how a major grocery chain can't keep their inventory stocked properly. It's all automated now, right? My buddy Mark was telling me about this new supply chain software his company is implementing, and it uses AI to predict buying patterns based on weather and local events. Like, if it's going to rain, it automatically orders more umbrellas and soup. It's actually kind of creepy when you think about it. The computers know what we want before we even know we want it. It's just like how you talk about something near your phone, and suddenly you're getting ads for it on Instagram. I was literally just talking to my mom about getting a new coffee maker, and bam, ten different ads for espresso machines. I don't even drink espresso, it makes my heart race too much. But yeah, no, I haven't been depressed like that. Just regular bad days, you know?

He's this little Jack Russell terrier mix, super high energy usually, but then he'll just drop and start shaking. They have him on some kind of medication for it now, pheno-something, I think? But they have to hide the pill in a scoop of peanut butter or he'll just spit it right back out. Dogs are so smart like that. Like, they know when you're trying to trick them. My old roommate had a cat that figured out how to open the cabinets in the kitchen. We'd wake up and all the Tupperware would be all over the floor. We had to put child locks on everything, which was honestly super annoying because I could barely figure out how to open them myself when I was half asleep trying to get a bowl for cereal. I'm a big cereal guy. Cinnamon Toast Crunch is top tier, but honestly, a good bowl of Honey Nut Cheerios just hits different sometimes. They churn it slower, so there's less air whipped into it, which makes it denser and more flavorful. Plus they serve it at a slightly warmer temperature so your taste buds don't get numbed by the cold. It's fascinating how much science goes into food. Like baking—baking is basically just chemistry. If you mess up the ratio of baking soda to flour, your cookies turn out like little hockey pucks. My mom used to make these incredible chocolate chip cookies when I was a kid, but she never wrote the recipe down. She just kind of threw things in a bowl. I tried to recreate them once, and I totally forgot the vanilla extract. You wouldn't think one little teaspoon of liquid would make such a huge difference, but they tasted completely flat. Anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right, brain injuries. Yeah, no, nothing serious like that. Just the occasional bump on a car trunk.

patient.answer: Um... holding the same position? I mean, I guess sometimes when I get really overwhelmed with everything, I'll kind of just freeze up. Like, I'll catch myself standing in the kitchen with my coffee mug just hovering halfway to my mouth, and I won't even realize how long I've been standing there. Or I'll start walking this same little loop back and forth by the couch for no real reason. I actually got that couch at a thrift store, believe it or not. It's this really cool mid-century modern style, kind of a mustard yellow color. Mark hated it when I first brought it home. He said it looked like it belonged in a 1970s bowling alley, but I think it gives the living room character. Plus, it's surprisingly comfortable once you break it in. The only problem is the fabric is a magnet for pet hair, which is weird because I don't even have any pets. But somehow, every time I sit down in black sweatpants, I stand up looking like I just hugged a golden retriever. I've gone through so many of those sticky lint rollers. The ones from the dollar store are terrible, by the way. The paper just rips in these tiny diagonal strips instead of peeling off in one clean sheet, so you spend ten minutes just trying to find the edge. It's infuriating. But yeah, sometimes I just stand there with my coffee, or do the pacing thing by the couch when things feel like too much.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychomotor abnormalities include classic catatonic negativism, which would support catatonic schizophrenia over schizoaffective or bipolar depression.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about negativism (resisting movement or instructions), which is a symptom of catatonia. My symptom profile does not contain a manifestation for this specific behavior.

patient.answer: Resist when they try to move me? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, nobody's really tried to physically move me around like that. I live by myself, so there's not really anyone around to do that anyway. It's just me and the apartment, which honestly is getting a little cramped. I've been thinking about trying to find a bigger place, maybe something with a balcony. I saw this one listing online the other day that had this amazing little terrace overlooking a courtyard, but the rent was just outrageous. It's crazy how much they charge for a tiny square of outdoor space in this city. And the deposit they wanted was equal to two months' rent, plus a non-refundable application fee. Application fees are such a scam. You pay fifty bucks just for them to run a credit check that costs them like two dollars, and then they don't even call you back if they pick someone else. I had a friend who spent almost three hundred dollars just applying to places before she finally got one. She works at a bakery downtown—well, she used to, before they downsized. She made these amazing sourdough loaves. Sourdough is so tricky to get right, you have to feed the starter every day and keep it at the perfect temperature. If it gets too cold, the yeast just kind of goes to sleep and the bread turns out flat. I tried making it once during that phase when everyone was baking bread, but my starter just smelled like old gym socks, so I threw it out. But anyway, no, nobody has tried to physically move me or anything like that. I just do my own thing.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a distinct manic episode, which would separate bipolar disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum causes of psychosis and catatonic symptoms.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually important or powerful?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about grandiose delusions or manic symptoms (feeling unusually important or powerful), which are not part of my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Important or powerful? No, definitely not. I mean, I'm just a customer service rep, you know? You pretty much feel like the least important person on the planet when you're doing that job. People call in and yell at you over the smallest things, acting like *they're* the king of the world. Like this one guy last week, he was screaming at me because his account update was delayed by an hour. An hour! And it's not like I personally control the servers. 

Speaking of servers, my laptop has been acting so weird lately. The fan just spins up and sounds like an airplane taking off, even when I only have one browser tab open. I think it might be full of dust. I tried to buy one of those cans of compressed air to clean it out, but they lock them up behind glass at the pharmacy now. You have to press a little red button and wait for an employee to come unlock it. I stood there for like fifteen minutes the other day, pressing the button, and the overhead speaker just kept saying "Customer assistance needed in aisle four." Over and over. Nobody ever came. I ended up just giving up and buying a candy bar at the front register instead. It was one of those ones with the almonds in it. I usually prefer peanuts, but peanuts have been giving me heartburn lately. Actually, almost everything gives me heartburn lately, which sucks because I love spicy food. There's this great Thai place down the street... 

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, feeling powerful. Yeah, no, I don't get feelings like that. I'm just a regular guy.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have been present continuously for at least one month, to distinguish schizophrenia from schizophreniform disorder and support the leading diagnosis among current candidates.

patient.answer:
Um, a month? No, it's been a lot longer than that. I think... yeah, it's been about a year and eight months now that I've been hearing them and knowing the software is watching me. And it's not just when I'm feeling really down or anything, it's just kind of always there. 

Like, even when I had that brief period where I tried to get back into running—which didn't last long, by the way. I bought these really expensive running shoes, the kind with the extra thick foam on the bottom that are supposed to be like running on clouds. They were neon green. I thought maybe a bright color would motivate me to put them on in the mornings. But the laces were those weird elastic ones that you don't tie, you just pull them tight with a little plastic toggle thing. I could never get the tension right. They were either cutting off the circulation to my toes or slipping off my heel with every step. I ended up getting this massive blister on my right heel after just two miles. Blisters are the worst, especially when you have to wear dress shoes for a cousin's wedding or something. My cousin Sarah got married last October in this beautiful outdoor ceremony, but it rained the whole time. They had to rent this huge tent at the last minute, and the ground was so muddy. Everyone's shoes were ruined. They had a taco bar for the reception, though, which was pretty cool. I love tacos, especially the al pastor kind with the little pieces of pineapple mixed in. The sweetness really balances out the spice. 

But yeah, anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the voices and the software thing. Yeah, it's been going on for like a year and eight months, not just when I'm super depressed.

doctor.intent: Determine whether prominent catatonic signs beyond psychomotor slowing/agitation are present, which would support catatonic schizophrenia over schizoaffective disorder or bipolar depression.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about mutism (going completely mute and stopping speaking), which is a catatonic symptom not covered by the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Go mute? Like, just stop talking entirely? No, I don't think so. I mean, I talk all day for my job, so I can't really get away with that. Though sometimes I definitely wish I could just hit a mute button on myself, or on the customers. My throat gets so dry by the end of my shift. I started drinking that throat coat tea, the one with the slippery elm in it? It's supposed to be really good for your vocal cords, but it tastes exactly like black licorice. 

I absolutely hate black licorice. When I was a kid, my grandma used to keep this crystal bowl of black jelly beans on her coffee table. Who even likes the black jelly beans? They just sat there for years, I swear they were practically fossilized. Her house always smelled like mothballs and peppermint. She had this massive grandfather clock in the hallway that chimed every fifteen minutes, day and night. It drove me crazy when I had to sleep over. The pendulum was made of this really shiny brass, and I remember trying to polish it with my sleeve once. Brass tarnishes so fast if you don't keep up with it. I have a brass lamp on my desk right now, actually, and it's looking pretty dull. I should probably buy some Brasso. You can get it at the hardware store, but the mom-and-pop hardware store near my apartment just closed down last month. They're turning it into a boutique pet bakery. A bakery for dogs! Can you believe people spend eight dollars on a cupcake for a pug? It's wild. 

But anyway... no, I don't ever just go completely mute. I always answer when people talk to me, even if it's just to say yeah or whatever.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms are accompanied by prominent negative symptoms, which would help distinguish schizophrenia (F20.2) from schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder with psychotic features, and organic catatonia.

patient.answer:
Lost interest? I guess... I mean, my friends keep telling me I sound totally flat these days, like I'm hard to read or something. And even when they're talking about stuff I actually care about, I just end up giving these really short answers and I avoid making plans to hang out. 

Making plans is just so exhausting anyway. You have to coordinate schedules, and then someone always cancels at the last minute because they forgot they had a dentist appointment. I hate the dentist. The last time I went, the hygienist kept talking to me while she had her hands in my mouth. How are you supposed to answer when someone has a metal hook scraping your molars? She was telling me all about her son's travel baseball team. Travel sports are so intense now. Parents spend thousands of dollars just so their ten-year-old can play in tournaments three states away every weekend. It's ridiculous. I played little league when I was a kid, but we just played at the park down the street. The snack shack there had the best soft pretzels. They were always super salty, and they came with this little plastic cup of neon yellow cheese. I used to dip my pretzels in it until the cheese was totally gone, and then I'd try to scrape the rest out with my finger. You can't really get good pretzels like that anymore, except maybe at the mall. But the mall is always so crowded, especially around the holidays. The parking lot is a nightmare... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, being around people. Yeah, I just kind of keep to myself and give short answers now. I don't really make plans with anyone.

patient.answer:
Freeze in the same position? I mean... I don't know about staying completely frozen like a statue for a really long time. But when I get really overwhelmed with everything, I do catch myself doing weird things. Like, I'll be standing in the kitchen with my coffee mug just hovering halfway to my mouth, just kind of stuck there. Or I'll find myself walking the exact same little loop around my couch over and over for no real reason. 

My couch is this dark gray sectional I got off Craigslist a couple years ago. The guy who sold it to me said it was barely used, but there's definitely a dip in the middle cushion where you can tell someone sat all the time. It came with these terrible mustard yellow throw pillows that I immediately threw in the closet. Mustard yellow is just such an aggressive color, you know? It reminds me of the uniform I had to wear at my first job in high school. I worked at this hot dog stand at the local fairgrounds. We had to wear these bright yellow polo shirts with a cartoon hot dog embroidered on the pocket. The hot dog was wearing sunglasses and giving a thumbs up. It was so embarrassing. The worst part was that the stand didn't have air conditioning, and in August it would get up to like a hundred degrees in there. The smell of boiling hot dogs and stale buns just baked into my clothes. I must have washed that uniform a hundred times, but I could never get the smell out. I actually had to throw the shirts away when I quit because even my mom said they were making the whole laundry room smell like cheap meat. I haven't been able to eat a hot dog since then. 

But yeah, what were we talking about? Oh, freezing. Yeah, I just kind of get stuck holding my coffee or pacing around the couch sometimes when it's all too much.

patient.answer:
Placed my arms in a position? Like... like someone else moving my body for me? No, nobody does that. I live by myself, so there's no one around to even try that, you know? It's just me and my cat, Barnaby. 

Barnaby is a Maine Coon mix, so he's absolutely massive. He's got these giant tufted ears and paws the size of baseballs. He's actually the reason I had to buy a new vacuum cleaner last month. He sheds so much, it's like a second cat is forming on my rug every week. I ended up getting one of those Dyson stick vacuums. They're so expensive, but everyone says they're the best. I don't know though, the battery only lasts like twenty minutes on the highest setting. By the time I finish the living room and the hallway, it's dead. Then I have to wait three hours for it to charge just so I can do my bedroom. It's so annoying. I should have just bought a regular plug-in one. My mom has this old Hoover from the nineties that still works perfectly. It's this ugly teal color, and it's super loud, but it sucks up everything. She used to make me vacuum the stairs every Saturday morning when I was a teenager. The cord was never quite long enough to reach all the way to the top, so I always had to unplug it halfway up and find another outlet. We lived in this split-level house, and the layout was just so weird. The kitchen was basically on a landing between the living room and the bedrooms...

Wait, sorry. No, nobody poses my arms or anything like that. I just move myself.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychosis is accompanied by clear prominent catatonic features, which would separate catatonic schizophrenia from schizophrenia with persistent psychosis but only mild psychomotor symptoms.
doctor.question: Have you ever repeated other people's words exactly after they say them?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about echolalia (repeating other people's words), which is not part of the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Repeated other people's words? Like, repeating them back? No, I don't think I do that. Unless you count when I'm on the phone at work. I work in customer service for this internet provider, and we actually have to repeat the customer's issue back to them as part of our script. It's supposed to show "active listening" or whatever. So if they say, "My router keeps dropping the signal," I have to say, "I understand your router keeps dropping the signal." 

It honestly just makes people mad half the time. They think I'm being condescending. People get so angry about their internet. I had this one guy yell at me for twenty minutes last week because his Netflix was buffering. He kept saying he paid for high speed and I was personally stealing from him. He lived out in this super rural area, too. Like, you can't live in the middle of a forest and expect gigabit speeds, you know? I actually went camping in a forest once, up in the mountains. It was supposed to be this relaxing weekend, but it rained the entire time. The tent leaked, and all my extra socks got soaked. There is nothing worse than wet socks. We tried to make a fire, but the wood was completely saturated. We ended up just sitting in my friend's car eating cold cans of baked beans and listening to the radio. They were playing this weird marathon of 80s synth-pop... 

But no, I don't just repeat what people say to me in normal life. Just when my boss makes me.

opening_question.question: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms for about 1 year and 8 months, including auditory hallucinations and a fixed delusional belief about work software monitoring/flagging him, occurring during periods of normal mood and without evidence of manic or major depressive episodes. He also shows catatonic features with marked psychomotor slowing, pacing/agitation, and episodes of freezing/posturing-like behavior. No seizure history, brain injury, or neurological illness supports excluding an organic catatonic disorder. This pattern is most consistent with catatonic schizophrenia.
